name: blkid
description: Locates and prints block device attributes: filesystem type, UUID, and label — the source for /etc/fstab entries.

flags.description: All detected partitions with TYPE, UUID, LABEL.

examples.output:
/dev/sda1: UUID="4F0B-1A2C" TYPE="vfat" PARTUUID="..."
/dev/sda2: UUID="8c1e4d2a-..." TYPE="ext4"
/dev/sdb1: UUID="a1b2c3d4-..." TYPE="xfs"
examples.explanation: Every partition with its filesystem and UUID. UUIDs are what /etc/fstab should reference — device names can change between boots.
Extracts just the UUID for use in scripts and fstab lines.

about: blkid uses libblkid to probe partitions. UUIDs persist across device renames (sdb becoming sdc), which is why fstab, GRUB, and systemd mount units reference them. lsblk -f shows the same data in tree form.
mistakes: Using device names (/dev/sdb1) in fstab — they can change; use UUID=.
